name: omniMux
description: Self-hosted music server with a Spotify-style PWA — search YouTube, save tracks to your own library, and stream from anywhere. AutoDJ crossfades, visualizers, multi-device sync. Navidrome + FastAPI + SvelteKit.

paragraphs: A self-hosted music server that lets you search YouTube, cache tracks to your library, and stream everything through a Spotify-like PWA. Built on top of Navidrome with a FastAPI middleware layer and a SvelteKit frontend.
Live demo → omnimux.wwel.sh (guest access, read-only library)

Streaming services rent you access to music you'll never own, lock your library behind monthly fees, and vanish the moment licensing deals fall through. omniMux flips that: search YouTube, keep the files on your own hardware, and stream them from anywhere over a PWA you install once. No cloud. No subscription. No gatekeepers. Just your music, on your server.
features: Beat-locked crossfades, tempo matching, and realistic pitch/speed slop — plus 10+ music visualizers driven by high-res iTunes album art.
Find any track and cache it locally. Topic channel results rank first for clean, official-quality audio.
Browse an artist's local albums alongside their full YouTube discography in one unified view.
Paste a YouTube playlist URL — omniMux queues all tracks and builds a matching Navidrome playlist automatically.
Every download is analysed for mood, BPM, energy, and key via mood-detector.

whatItDoes.text: A self-hosted music server that lets you search YouTube, cache tracks to your library, and stream everything through a Spotify-like PWA. Built on top of Navidrome with a FastAPI middleware layer and a SvelteKit frontend.

requirements.text: On first run, open Navidrome at :4533, create an admin account, then log into the omniMux web app with those same credentials.
